newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN WOOL PUTS ASIA IN ITS NEW-PRODUCT FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN WOOL PUTS ASIA IN ITS NEW-PRODUCT FOCUS.

text.p: The Australian wool industry's attempt to stage a comeback in world markets through the development of innovative fine-wool products has switched its focus to North Asia, the International Wool Secretariat (IWS) said on Thursday.
In Japan, super merino rugs, velvet pile merino carpets and terry-like wool bed covers were currently being developed, it said in a statement.
A machine washable pure merino wool under-futon also had been launched in South Korea, it said.
Lightness and luxury in wool were in demand in Asia, the IWS said.
The IWS statement was issued as part of an Australian Merino Bicentenary held here on Thursday.
The IWS promoted 200th birthday celebrations for Australia's leading wool export in conjunction with Australia Post, which launched two special commemorative merino postage stamps.
Faced with a declining market in recent years, the Australian wool industry has been developing finer wool types, including lightweight wool.
Australia exports about A$3.8 billion worth of wool a year.
About 80 percent of all merino sheep are reared in Australia, which supplies one-third of the world's wool and one-half of its merino wool.
The first flock of merino sheep arrived in Australia from South Africa in 1797, nine years after the first British settlement in 1788.
The flock was originally from Spain, where merino sheep originated, IWS said.
